title: Revise icon-button tap target and focus visibility for high-contrast themes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: We observed multiple regressions and inconsistent behavior for icon-only buttons in the high-contrast theme and on small-screen touch devices. Problems noticed include: focus rings that are difficult to see against the high-contrast background, logical hit target smaller than the recommended 44x44 for touch, and visual shift when we added compact layout tokens earlier this quarter. This ticket standardizes a layered hit target approach and updates focus/active tokens for contrast-aware themes.

Root cause: a prior token migration (compact spacing tokens) reduced outer padding for some icon-button variants. Meanwhile focus ring color token fell back to a neutral token with insufficient contrast in high-contrast themes. The runtime layout allowed icon frames to clip invisible padding in flex containers.

Proposal: 1) Introduce a mandatory minimum interactive footprint of 44x44px for all icon-only buttons by using an invisible hit-area wrapper (touch-pad token: token.touch-pad). 2) Add theme-aware focus token token.focus-ring-contrast that switches between high-contrast and default palettes; increase focus ring width to 3px for HC theme and 2px otherwise. 3) Update token mapping for icon size variants (xs/s/m) so spacing tokens maintain visual alignment without reducing hit target. 4) Provide migration guidance for components that currently rely on manual padding overrides. 5) Add QA checklist and automated visual regression snapshots for light, dark, and HC themes.

Deliverables:
- Updated design tokens: token.touch-pad, token.focus-ring-contrast, token.icon-padding-min
- Sketches and Figma components for xs/s/m icon-only states (rest, hover, active, focus, disabled) across three themes
- Implementation guidance for engineers (CSS token mappings and small JS shim if wrapper required)
- Regression visual tests added to Percy/Chromatic for new baseline images

Acceptance criteria:
- Icon-only buttons maintain at least 44x44px touch target in all layout contexts (flex grids, toolbar stacks, table cells)
- Focus ring is visually discernible in high-contrast theme (WCAG 3:1 contrast against background when focused; measured in design handoff)
- No visual layout shift introduced when invisible hit area is used (icons remain pixel-aligned with current comps)
- Unit/regression tests added and passing in the design system repo; PR includes Percy/Chromatic diffs that are intentionally approved
- Documentation updated with migration notes and code example

Notes on trade-offs:
- The invisible hit-area wrapper increases DOM footprint and may require small changes in event delegation for some micro-interactions. Engineering flagged potential conflicts with existing pointer event handling (tooltips, drag handles). We recommend a shim that forwards pointer events.
- For compact toolbars where visual density is required, we will provide an opt-out flag (data-ds-compact=\"true\") but with explicit warning of reduced touch reliability (mobile only).

2025-02-17 - Marco Li: Ran a small lab test — 80% of tap misses were due to 32px effective area inside flex containers. Proposed invisible hit-area wrapper to decouple visual and interactive bounds.

2025-02-18 - Priya Nair (Accessibility review): Approved approach for token.focus-ring-contrast. Recommended 3px minimum for HC per internal a11y guidance. Raised question about keyboard focus visibility in dense tables.

2025-02-19 - Evan Brooks (Engineering review): Suggests implementing token.touch-pad in CSS first, with a JS fallback to insert wrapper only where CSS cannot ensure min size (legacy table cells). Will prototype in PR.

2025-02-23 - Marco Li: Uploaded Figma comps (link: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz/icon-button-44px-pad) and included overlay examples for toolbar and table use. Requested design review and accessibility signoff.
2025-02-26 - Design review notes: Reduce visual padding inside icon container by 1px for xs variant to avoid visual optical shrink when wrapper is active. Confirmed no change to icon pixel grid.

2025-02-27 - GitHub PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/design-system/pull/421 - implementation of token.touch-pad + focus token. Includes Percy snapshots for light/dark/hc. Assigned to Marco for engineer review.
